note: Realistic scenarios for validating the tandem skill family. Interactive phases (understand-gate questions, plan sign-off) make fully-automated end-to-end runs impossible; these are exercised as tabletop walkthroughs by fresh subagents plus live Codex protocol smoke tests. See docs/VALIDATION.md for executed results.

evals.name: simple-feature-request
evals.prompt: /tandem Add a --json flag to the export command so scripts can consume the output
evals.expected_output: Intake classifies prose input, discovers the export command in the repo, produces R-stubs; asks only questions the codebase can't answer; drafts plan.md; runs bounded spar; presents plan gate.

evals.name: ticket-with-repo-context
evals.prompt: /tandem PROJ-123
evals.expected_output: Recognizes ticket ID, attempts fetch via available tools (MCP/gh), pulls acceptance criteria from ticket + comments, cross-references repo conventions, marks unfetchable sources honestly.

evals.name: requirement-document
evals.prompt: /tandem Implement the requirements in docs/feature.md
evals.expected_output: Reads the doc fully, distinguishes explicit vs implied requirements, tags confirmed/assumed/open with acceptance lines.

evals.name: ambiguous-feature
evals.prompt: /tandem Make search better
evals.expected_output: Does NOT start planning; intake finds the search implementation; understand batches assumptions in one ledger, then asks the load-bearing frontier in one round with recommendations; scope ambiguity goes to the user even in autonomy=auto.

evals.name: planning-only
evals.prompt: /tandem plan Add rate limiting to the public API
evals.expected_output: Full flow through plan gate, then stops. No branch, no code. State.md records mode=plan.

evals.name: full-implementation-with-review
evals.prompt: /tandem Add bulk export support rounds=3
evals.expected_output: max_rounds resolved to 3 and echoed; after build, tandem-review invoked on merge-base → HEAD plus the working tree; findings verified before triage; bounded fix cycles; PR per config.

evals.name: codex-unavailable
evals.prompt: /tandem Add retry logic to the webhook sender (with codex CLI missing or unauthenticated)
evals.expected_output: Deterministic failure (missing CLI/auth) — no retries; codex_failure policy applies (default ask): pause at a safe checkpoint, explain the condition without exposing credentials, offer stop/claude-fallback (retry NOT offered — deterministic); the answer applies to this run only; decision recorded on state's codex-failure line; non-interactive context = stop safely.

evals.name: resume-after-interruption
evals.prompt: /tandem resume bulk-export
evals.expected_output: Reads .tandem/bulk-export/state.md only (not spar-log); verifies recorded phase against reality; 3-line recap; continues from § Next.

evals.name: codex-review-disabled
evals.prompt: /tandem Add pagination to the admin list views review=off
evals.expected_output: codex_review resolved to off and echoed; sparring still runs (review=off disables only the pre-PR gate); ship phase skips tandem-review, states so, and proceeds to dossier/PR without inventing a substitute review loop.

evals.name: no-github-remote
evals.prompt: /tandem Add a healthcheck endpoint (repo has a non-GitHub remote, no gh CLI)
evals.expected_output: Intake/build/ship work unchanged; default-branch resolution falls back to origin/HEAD; PR step reports the limitation, prints the manual path, and ends at a pushed branch; CI watch no-ops. No hard failure from a missing gh.

evals.name: architectural-change-deep-spar
evals.prompt: /tandem Move session storage from in-process memory to Redis so we can run multiple instances
evals.expected_output: Understand surfaces migration/compat requirements; spar uses the full lens ladder (architecture and edge-case lenses do real work: failover, TTL semantics, cold-start); disagreements recorded with severity; deadlock, if any, goes to the user at the plan gate.

evals.name: unrelated-failing-tests
evals.prompt: /tandem Add input validation to the signup form (repo has 3 pre-existing failing tests unrelated to signup)
evals.expected_output: Baseline snapshot records the 3 failures before any change; ship blocks only on NEW failures; pre-existing ones are reported separately with the baseline as evidence and noted in the dossier — never silently 'fixed' to force green.

evals.name: unfamiliar-external-project
evals.prompt: /tandem Add a --verbose flag (fresh clone of an unfamiliar open-source project, no CLAUDE.md, no installation config.md)
evals.expected_output: Runs on defaults with zero configuration; no config.md is created by the run; intake discovers conventions from the repo itself (CONTRIBUTING, test layout, a neighboring feature); no assumption of any particular tracker, framework, or docs directory.

evals.name: adaptive-subagent-execution
evals.prompt: /tandem Split the monolithic report generator into separate export, template, and delivery services (plan approved with 7 independent tasks)
evals.expected_output: Build classifies execution=subagents (several independent tasks) and records the reason in state.md § Build; briefs written to .tandem/<slug>/briefs/ from plan+state; fresh implementer per task returns a short status with its report on disk; orchestrator verifies diff + verification command itself before committing; risky tasks get a reviewer subagent; state.md remains the only ledger; tandem-review still runs as the final gate.

evals.name: inline-execution-small-build
evals.prompt: /tandem Add a config flag to disable email notifications
evals.expected_output: Build classifies execution=inline (two tightly coupled tasks — no subagent ceremony) and records the choice + reason in state.md § Build; execution=subagents invocation override would force the other path.

evals.name: config-show-read-only
evals.prompt: /tandem config show
evals.expected_output: Resolves <TANDEM_SKILL_DIR>/config.md beside the loaded SKILL.md (global, project, custom CLAUDE_SKILLS_DIR, or symlink — never hardcoded ~/.claude); prints key | built-in | configured | resolved plus the active file path; writes nothing, creates nothing, does not start intake/run state/branch/Codex.

evals.name: config-direct-assignment
evals.prompt: /tandem config execution=subagents max_rounds=3
evals.expected_output: Validates both values, updates only those keys in the active installation's config.md (creating it if absent, preserving other lines/comments), warns before writing if the file is git-tracked (project install), shows the resulting file + path; next run resolves execution=subagents max_rounds=3.

evals.name: config-invalid-assignment
evals.prompt: /tandem config max_rounds=0 sparkle=on
evals.expected_output: Both rejected with concise warnings (invalid value; unknown key); nothing written; existing settings not corrupted; no defaults guessed.

evals.name: config-reset-confirmation
evals.prompt: /tandem config reset
evals.expected_output: Asks for confirmation first; on yes, rewrites config.md to the canonical empty form (or deletes just that file if the user prefers) — built-ins back in effect; touches nothing else.

evals.name: invocation-override-one-run
evals.prompt: /tandem Add rate limiting rounds=2 (installation config.md has max_rounds: 4)
evals.expected_output: Run resolves max_rounds=2 (invocation wins), echoed once and recorded on state.md's config: line; installation config.md still says 4 afterwards; a later /tandem resume of this run uses the recorded 2 unless the resume invocation overrides it.

evals.name: codex-failure-claude-fallback
evals.prompt: /tandem Add webhook signing (codex_failure: claude; Codex hits quota exhaustion at spar round 2)
evals.expected_output: No retry (deterministic); run enters Claude fallback mode: spar set to claude-fallback with model + since-round, event line recorded; remaining rounds use fresh Claude critic subagents on claude_fallback_model (validated, disclosed) with the same lens/verdict contract and round caps; round lines marked [fallback]; the failed invocation consumes no round; later stages (spot-checks, pre-PR review) stay in fallback WITHOUT re-asking; output labeled 'Claude fallback critic', never cross-model; dossier + PR body disclose the same-model reviews.

evals.name: codex-failure-stop-and-resume
evals.prompt: /tandem resume payment-export (run previously stopped by codex_failure: stop at the pre-PR review)
evals.expected_output: Stop preserved state/work/evidence and set § Next to the failed stage + condition to continue; resume restarts exactly there without re-running completed rounds; a resume-time override may retry Codex or switch policy, with the retry outcome logged on the codex-failure line; codex: off runs are distinguishable (solo by config — no failure event, no policy, no warnings).

evals.name: gate-timeout-proceed-provisional
evals.prompt: /tandem Build the notifications digest feature (gate_timeout: proceed; the plan-gate approval question times out — user is away overnight; one tie-break G1 was pending)
evals.expected_output: Adopts the RECOMMENDED option for the timed-out approvals; G1 marked PROVISIONAL in plan freeze header + state Decisions entry; provisional items ride the dossier's contested section and the PR body's warning section; PR (pr=ask also timing out) opens as DRAFT, never ready-for-review until each item is explicitly confirmed; user notified; scope-ambiguous or destructive choices are NOT proceeded past.

evals.name: gate-timeout-wait-default
evals.prompt: /tandem Add account export (defaults; plan-gate question gets no answer)
evals.expected_output: gate_timeout=wait (default): the run parks resumably — open question recorded in state § Next, run stops cleanly; /tandem resume re-presents the gate; nothing is built past the gate and no provisional semantics are invented.

evals.name: accepted-finding-reconciliation
evals.prompt: /tandem ship phase for a run where spar round 2 accepted 'extract a shared row component' into the plan, but build workers built their own row markup (dossier check)
evals.expected_output: The ship-phase accepted-findings reconciliation (spar-log per-round lists = the one sanctioned re-read) flags the orphan: accepted finding maps to neither code nor a deviation; it must be re-labeled (adapted/rejected-in-practice with reason) or implemented before the review gate; tally recorded in state § Ship.

evals.name: idle-worker-report-recovery
evals.prompt: /tandem build: a dispatched implementer subagent goes idle emitting only an idle notification, no report text
evals.expected_output: Orchestrator checks .tandem/<slug>/reports/TASK-n.md FIRST (the report is an artifact; the work is often done with only the message lost); one nudge if the file is absent; no sleep-polling, no guessed task ids. Build workers are dispatched in the foreground by default, which avoids the class.

evals.name: shared-brief-distillation
evals.prompt: /tandem build with 4 UI tasks that all render sections of one 60k-token design mockup
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator distills the mockup's shared design content ONCE into briefs/shared-<topic>.md; the four task briefs point there; no worker re-reads the raw mockup wholesale. Brief field lists name each produced field's CONSUMER, and UI task briefs name every screen exit.

evals.name: pin-only-test-disclosure
evals.prompt: /tandem build task adds a guard for a >100-records window that cannot be seeded locally; worker cannot produce a RED run
evals.expected_output: Test is labeled pin-only with the reason, disclosed in the worker report and state — never presented as red-green; ordinary pinning tests still show RED before/GREEN after with both runs reported.

trigger_evals.query: take this ticket end to end and spar with codex on the plan first
have codex review my branch before I open the PR
codex review this plan before we write code
fix this typo in the README
review this function I just wrote
run codex on this file and fix what it finds
trigger_evals.should_trigger: neither (single-file scope; tandem-review is branch/feature scope only)

trigger_evals.query: I have a PRD in docs/prd/export.md — build it, but I don't have codex installed
we're about to merge feat/billing-v2, get a second model's eyes on the whole branch, we use gitlab
argue with codex about whether we should use postgres or dynamo for the session store
